header:
Date: 2027-03-10
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Srinivasan (Redwood SE), Michael Chen (BlueRock CISO), Lena Ortiz (BlueRock VP Eng), Tom Alvarez (BlueRock Network Eng), Rita Gomez (BlueRock Compliance)
Notes: Private/VPC on-prem security deep dive focused on network isolation, ingress/egress, firewalling, encryption/KMS and audit requirements.
summary: Redwood and BlueRock walked through Private deployment network architecture. Main concerns: locked-down ingress, strict egress controls, KMS integration (BYOK vs Redwood-managed), audit logs and SIEM integration, SOC 2 expectations and proof points. SE discussed bastion/NAT patterns, private endpoints, VPC peering, flow logs, and RBAC/SSO mapping. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share detailed architecture diagram and Terraform examples; BlueRock to provide CIDRs and SOC 2 questions.
topics: Ingress patterns: private ALB vs bastion + port forwarding
Egress filtering, NAT, and controlled outbound API access
Firewalling: security groups, NACLs, inline firewalls and WAF
Private endpoints, VPC peering, transitive routing concerns
Encryption & KMS: BYOK, HSM, key rotation, envelope encryption
Audit logs, flow logs, retention, SIEM integration (Splunk/Elastic)
RBAC/SSO: SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, least-privilege roles
SOC 2 / ISO evidence and compliance artifacts
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll just do a quick intros, then Priya will take us through the private VPC pattern.
[00:08] Michael: hi, Michael Chen here, CISO at BlueRock. we've got some strict egress and data residency requirements so hope to drill into that.
[00:14] Lena: lena, VP Eng, here to cover infra constraints.
[00:19] Priya: great, thanks. I'm Priya, SE on Redwood. quick note: apologies if audio stutters, connection looks fine on our end.
[00:27] Priya: K, first slide — recommended deployment: customer-managed VPC with Redwood worker instances in private subnets, control plane can be either Redwood-hosted with private peering or customer-hosted depending on compliance.
[00:42] Tom: when you say control plane peering, do you mean cross-account VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink?
[00:48] Priya: good question — we support both. for the highest isolation we recommend PrivateLink / interface endpoints so the control plane traffic flows over private ENIs, no internet egress. peering is possible but you have to be careful about transitive routing.
[01:05] Michael: we're SOC 2 Type II and ISO-aligned; auditors will ask for network diagrams, ingress/egress rules, and proof of key management. how do you surface those?
[01:15] Jordan: we have a security pack — architecture diagrams, SOC 2 scope, pen test summary. we'll send the artifact after this call.
[01:20] Priya: on the network side: we recommend three-layer subnetting: management, compute, and storage subnets. management has bastion + SSM, compute has Redwood workers in private subnets with no public IPs, storage subnets for object stores with VPC endpoints.
[01:36] Tom: do you require NAT for outbound model downloads or Docker pulls?
[01:42] Priya: yes, initial provisioning may need egress for image/model pulls. options: controlled egress via NAT gateway with egress-only firewall rules, or bake images into AMIs in your air-gapped environment to eliminate egress. for bootstrap we can support both.
[01:58] Lena: what about firewalling? we use strict SGs and NACLs; are there port requirements?
[02:05] Priya: minimal ports: outbound HTTPS to specific Redwood control-plane endpoints (if PrivateLink not used). Intra-VPC traffic between workers uses gRPC over TLS on configurable ports. We'll provide a hardened port list. Security groups + host-level firewall is recommended.
[02:20] Michael: KMS — do you support BYOK and HSM integration? ours is an HSM-backed KMS and we need key ownership.
[02:29] Priya: yes, we support BYOK and integration with customer KMS (AWS KMS with custom key store backed by CloudHSM, Google Cloud KMS, Azure KeyVault HV). in Private deployments you can configure Redwood to use your KMS for envelope keys. we also support rotating wrapping keys.
[02:44] Tom: any latency/ops impact with BYOK?
[02:47] Priya: slight additional latency on key unwrap but negligible compared to token generation; we cache decrypted keys in memory with TTL and use envelope encryption to limit calls to KMS.
[02:57] Michael: audit logs — we need immutable logs forwarded to our SIEM (Splunk). retention 7 years for certain artifacts. can you stream logs and provide tamper evidence?
[03:08] Jordan: yes, we can forward audit logs via syslog/HTTPS to your collector or deliver via S3 with write-once policies. for tamper evidence we provide audit log checksums and integrate with your SIEM.
[03:18] Priya: also flow logs: we recommend enabling VPC Flow Logs to your log bucket and hooking into your SIEM; Redwood produces application-level audit events (user actions, model versions, API keys usage) that you can ship.
[03:31] Lena: are there RBAC controls for developer vs ops vs admin?
[03:35] Priya: yes—RBAC with roles: Viewer, Operator, Admin, and custom roles. we map to SAML groups and support SCIM for provisioning. enforcement points: API tokens tied to roles, route-level RBAC in the console.
[03:49] Tom: for ingress — do you use private load balancers? we want no public entry points.
[03:55] Priya: we support internal ALBs only, and also TCP proxy with mTLS between customer ingress and Redwood workers. for management access we recommend SSM Session Manager or a bastion with strict authorized keys and short-lived certs.
[04:11] Michael: egress filtering — we need to block all outbound except to our approved endpoints. can Redwood work with an egress proxy?
[04:17] Priya: yes, we can route outbound through customer-managed egress proxy. we also support explicit allow lists for control-plane endpoints; when PrivateLink used, control-plane traffic stays internal. model downloads can be pinned to an internal registry to avoid public internet.
[04:31] Jordan: quick interjection — some customers choose to host a mirrored model repo inside their network to avoid all egress. we can provide tooling to sync models offline.
[04:40] Tom: firewalling specifics — do you recommend stateful SGs only or also NACLs?
[04:44] Priya: SGs for host-level fine-grain rules, NACLs for subnet-level defense-in-depth. for high-security setups we recommend both plus host-based firewalls and intrusion detection.
[04:56] Lena: what about private endpoints to AWS services like S3 and KMS? any special config?
[05:01] Priya: use VPC interface endpoints for S3 and KMS; restrict via resource policy to the VPC endpoints and the ARN of the Redwood IAM principal. we will provide example IAM policies and endpoint policies.
[05:14] Michael: auditors will ask about key rotation policies. what's Redwood's default?
[05:18] Priya: Redwood recommends rotating wrapping keys annually and data keys more frequently per your policy; with BYOK you control rotation. we also maintain key metadata in audit logs for rotation events.
[05:28] Jordan: circling back to SOC 2 evidence — we'll include architecture diagrams, control descriptions, pen test summaries, and you can request specific logs via the compliance pack.
[05:36] Rita: do you maintain egress snapshots? we have to show that certain services were not contacted.
[05:41] Priya: yes, we can produce egress traffic logs with timestamps and destination IPs; combining VPC Flow Logs and application audit logs should cover that.
[05:50] Tom: any extra networking gotchas for multi-AZ high availability?
[05:54] Priya: ensure subnets in each AZ have proper route tables, NATs or egress endpoints in each AZ to avoid cross-AZ chattiness. we also recommend placement groups for low-latency GPU clusters.
[06:06] Michael: what about penetration testing? are we allowed to run tests against the private deployment?
[06:12] Jordan: for private deployments you control the environment — you can run internal tests. if you plan to test Redwood-managed control plane, we request a coordinated window and a testing plan.
[06:22] Lena: SLA concerns — if we do Private with full isolation, what's the fallback if capacity issues arise?
[06:28] Priya: you can configure fallback policies: allow routing to a hosted read-only fallback or queue requests. enterprise contracts often include reserved capacity for predictable throughput. we'll include options in the follow-up.
[06:40] Tom: connection detail — do workers initiate outbound TLS to control-plane or is it mutual TLS inbound?
[06:46] Priya: typically workers establish a mutual TLS session to the control-plane endpoints, authenticated with client certs. with PrivateLink the traffic never leaves the AWS network.
[06:56] Michael: about SIEM integration — prefer Splunk HE or direct S3 ingestion.
[06:59] Priya: both supported; we can send logs to Splunk HEC, CloudWatch, or S3 with lifecycle and WORM policies.
[07:10] Jordan: any show-stoppers we should know about?
[07:13] Michael: main blocker is KMS BYOK plus proof of separation for keys and long-term retention for logs.
[07:19] Priya: we can support BYOK and provide the retention pipeline; we'll show config examples.
[07:24] Lena: timeline — we're aiming for a pilot in Q2; must pass security review before infra provisioning.
[07:30] Jordan: noted. we'll prioritize the compliance docs.
[07:34] Tom: quick question on RBAC and SSO — do you support role mapping to our AD groups?
[07:38] Priya: yes SAML with AD FS or Okta, group-to-role mapping, SCIM for provisioning; we also support short-lived API tokens minted via SSO.
[07:47] Michael: can we get encryption-at-rest evidence per table/volume?
[07:51] Priya: yes, we can provide volume-level encryption metadata and KMS key ARNs used for each volume; we include that in the audit logs.
[07:59] Rita: about data residency — we need storage only in our region and copies cannot leave. how is cross-region replication handled?
[08:06] Priya: by default we keep data in-region. replication is opt-in; for backups we can ensure they are stored in your region or in customer-managed buckets with no cross-region replication.
[08:17] Jordan: recap — Redwood to hand over: architecture diagram, hardened port list, KMS/BYOK guide, Terraform snippets, SOC2 pack. BlueRock to share: CIDRs, current KMS vendor details, SOC2 auditor questions.
[08:29] Michael: sounds good. thanks.
[08:32] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow-up with artifacts and set next review.
[08:35] [call ends]
